procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Nephrology letter from 11/25 reviewed: hemoglobin 9.0, low retic, anemia of CKD; epoetin started at dialysis. He says he still drags by midafternoon, 'maybe a little better.' No bleeding, black stools or chest pain. Sugars higher over the holidays, fasting up to 200s, no lows.

Exam: BP R arm as charted. Conjunctivae a little pale. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema. AVF thrill.

A/P
Anemia of CKD - on epoetin per dialysis unit; CBC today to see the trend.
T2DM - A1c today. Reviewed holiday eating; keep same insulin for now.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Mr. Washington - A1c 8.2, up from 7.9. Not alarming, but let's aim to bring it back down with steadier meals. Hemoglobin 9.4, a bit better than November. The epoetin takes a couple of months to work fully.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: 90-day refills sent for glargine pens, lispro pens, pen needles, lisinopril, atorvastatin and aspirin. Sevelamer is prescribed by nephrology - pharmacy redirected.

documents.title: Nephrology follow-up letter
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology group - follow-up note, date of service 03/09/2020 (transcription delayed; copy to PCP).

He returns about the tiredness first evaluated in the fall. Despite epoetin with dialysis he still feels worn out after a full night's sleep and cannot walk as far as he would like. No bleeding, no melena, no recent infections.

PMH: ESRD on HD MWF via L AVF; anemia of CKD; type 2 diabetes with suboptimal control; hypertension.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5, sevelamer 800 with meals, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40; epoetin alfa with HD.
Allergies: NKDA.

BP 146/88. Conjunctival pallor. Exam otherwise unremarkable. Neuro: nonfocal.

Labs (pre-HD): Hgb 10.2, Hct 31%, MCV 86, ferritin 220, serum iron 35.

Impression: anemia of CKD, improving on ESA, with iron-restricted erythropoiesis.
Plan: iron sucrose 100 mg IV with dialysis x 10 sessions; continue epoetin per protocol; repeat iron indices after the course.

documents.title: Appointment change
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Called pt to convert his May office visit to video given the pandemic. He has a tablet his daughter set up. Moved to 5/19 video visit. Reminded him dialysis unit precautions continue.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, patient at his kitchen table, daughter helped with the connection. Consent for telehealth given.

Says the kidney doctors 'gave me iron in the machine' this spring, a series of treatments, and he thinks his energy is a notch better. We have not received a note from that March nephrology visit yet - asked front desk to request it.
Dialysis going fine; unit screens everyone at the door. No fevers or cough. Sugars mostly 120s-180s fasting. No lows.
Home BP not checked.

Observed: comfortable, speaking in full sentences, no visible swelling.

A/P: anemia of CKD on epoetin plus IV iron per nephrology; ESRD on HD; T2DM on basal-bolus insulin. No changes. Labs at next in-person visit. RTC summer if the clinic is seeing people in person.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Diabetic eye exam 6/16/2020 (delayed from spring). Dilated fundus exam: no diabetic retinopathy, no macular edema, either eye. Early cataract, not affecting function. Next exam 1 year.

documents.author: nephrology
documents.body: Monthly pre-treatment labs from the dialysis unit, drawn 8/10/2020. Hemoglobin 10.6 on epoetin; iron course completed in April. Phosphorus 4.9. Remaining chemistries as listed. No changes to dialysis prescription.

documents.body: Called to set up his flu shot. Booked nurse visit 10/13, Tuesday afternoon. Reminded him masks are required in the building.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, not hungry, losing weight.

HPI: Over about two months he has felt steadily more worn down, and food doesn't appeal to him - eats half of what he used to. Weight down 10 lb (85 to 80.5 kg on our scale). Dialysis unit also noticed his target weight has had to come down. Denies cough, sputum, fever, sweats at night, chest pain, belly pain, change in stool, blood in stool. No sick contacts he knows of. Mood ok.

Exam: BP R arm as charted, afebrile. Thinner in the face. Breath sounds diminished over the right apex; no crackles or wheeze elsewhere. Heart regular, no murmur. Abdomen soft, nontender, no masses, no hepatosplenomegaly. No lymphadenopathy in neck, axillae. AVF good thrill. No edema.

A/P
Unintended weight loss with fatigue and anorexia, focal finding R apex, 40 pk-yr ex-smoker on dialysis.
- Chest x-ray, PA/lateral, tomorrow morning (no dialysis Tuesday).
- CBC with diff, A1c today.
- Will call him with the film. Low threshold for CT and ID/pulm depending on result.
Anemia of CKD and ESRD - per nephrology. T2DM - eating less, watch for lows; if fasting sugars under 90, call and we'll lower glargine.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest. Patchy airspace opacity in the right apex. No cavitation. No hilar or mediastinal widening. Left lung clear. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal.

documents.title: Chest x-ray
documents.author: radiology
documents.body: Right apical infiltrate without cavitation. Recommend clinical correlation; consider infectious etiology including mycobacterial infection given location.

documents.title: Chest x-ray result and ID referral
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Film shows an infiltrate at the top of the right lung, no cavity. With weight loss, apical location and dialysis, TB has to be ruled out first. Spoke with ID - they will see him 11/9 in the negative-pressure clinic room and collect sputum. Until then: wear a mask around others and at dialysis, and I notified the dialysis unit charge nurse so they can seat him in isolation. CBC: white count and platelets normal, hemoglobin 10.4, same as his usual. A1c 7.6. He understands. Daughter on speaker.

documents.title: Infectious Disease consultation
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
INFECTIOUS DISEASE CONSULTATION - outside ID clinic. Seen 11/09/2020. Requested by primary care for a right apical infiltrate.

HPI: 69-year-old man on maintenance hemodialysis with a prior anemia evaluation, referred for two months of worsening fatigue, poor appetite and a 10-pound weight loss he hadn't tried for. No cough, fevers or night sweats.
PMH: ESRD on HD (L AVF), anemia of CKD on ESA, type 2 diabetes on insulin, hypertension.
Meds: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro sliding scale, lisinopril 5 mg, sevelamer 800 mg with meals, aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, epoetin with HD.
Allergies: NKDA.
SH: quit smoking about ten years ago after 40 pack-years. Retired letter carrier.
FH: noncontributory.

Vitals: T 37.2 C (99 F), BP 150/90, HR 88, RR 16.
Exam: thin. Reduced breath sounds at the right apex; no crackles, no wheezes. Remainder unremarkable.

Data: CBC from 10/26 - normal white count and platelets, Hgb at his baseline. Creatinine at his dialysis baseline. Chest radiograph 10/27 personally reviewed: right apical infiltrate, no cavity.

Seen in an airborne isolation room. Induced sputum x3 collected 11/10-11/11.
Addendum 11/12: specimen 1 AFB smear positive (1+); MTB complex NAAT detected; rpoB mutation not detected. HIV Ag/Ab nonreactive.

Impression: pulmonary tuberculosis, drug-susceptible by molecular testing, in a hemodialysis patient.
Plan:
- Start 11/13: isoniazid 300 mg daily, rifampin 600 mg daily, pyridoxine 50 mg daily; pyrazinamide 2,000 mg and ethambutol 1,200 mg three times weekly given after each dialysis (renal dosing). Directly observed therapy through the local health department; dialysis unit nurses to observe the post-HD doses.
- Case reported to the health department; contact evaluation by them.
- Airborne precautions at dialysis until three negative smears.
- Monthly visual acuity/color checks on ethambutol; LFTs monthly.
- Rifampin can lower the effect of several drugs; reviewed his list - no major issue, monitor sugars.
- Follow-up in ID clinic in 8 weeks.

documents.title: Health department call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Public health nurse called to introduce herself; she is managing DOT for Mr. Washington's TB treatment. Daily doses observed by video on non-dialysis days, in person at the unit after dialysis. Asked if anyone in our office had close prolonged contact - only the 10/26 visit, he was masked, room cleaned. She will handle household contact testing. ID consult letter received 11/23 and routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ID letter reviewed. Pulmonary TB on four-drug therapy via DOT. Med list updated with ID's regimen. Video check-in mid-December.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, at home. About a month into TB treatment. Taking every dose with the health dept nurse watching. Orange urine and tears - expected with rifampin, he was warned. Mild nausea on the big pill days, eats crackers first. Appetite starting to come back. No yellowing, no belly pain, no vision change. Sugars a little higher, 150s-210s fasting, no lows.

Appears well, in good spirits. Speech normal.

A/P: pulmonary TB on 4 drugs, tolerating; LFTs and vision by ID. T2DM: no change for now; call if consistently over 250. ID follow-up January. Next in-person visit once he's cleared from airborne precautions.

documents.title: Infectious Disease follow-up
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic follow-up, seen 01/12/2021.
Two months of four-drug therapy completed by DOT, no missed doses. Appetite improving, weight coming back. Nausea resolved.
Culture from 11/10: M. tuberculosis complex, susceptible to all first-line agents. Sputum 1/5/2021 smear negative; prior two smears in December also negative. Released from airborne precautions.
LFTs normal through the intensive phase. Visual acuity and color vision unchanged.
Plan: stop pyrazinamide and ethambutol as of today. Continue isoniazid 300 mg, rifampin 600 mg and pyridoxine 50 mg daily for 4 more months (end date mid-May 2021). End-of-treatment chest film. Return May.

documents.title: Dialysis unit records
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body: Dialysis unit fax: COVID-19 vaccine (Pfizer) given in the unit 1/29/2021 and 2/19/2021. March monthly labs attached; Hgb 10.7. Note: patient remains on TB continuation-phase meds per ID, observed doses after treatments.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Back in person. Smear-negative, off airborne precautions since January per ID. On isoniazid, rifampin, pyridoxine until May. Eating well again; weight 82 kg, up from 80.5. Energy fair. Both COVID shots done at dialysis. Sugars 140s-200 fasting.

Exam: BP as charted, afebrile. Lungs: still slightly reduced at the R apex, otherwise clear. Heart regular. No edema. AVF thrill.

A/P
Pulmonary TB - continuation phase, per ID.
T2DM - A1c today. Not changing insulin while on rifampin; reassess after TB treatment ends.
ESRD/anemia - per nephrology.
RTC June.

documents.title: Refill authorization
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Refill request: insulin glargine, insulin lispro, test strips. Sent 90-day supply. Pharmacy asked whether to fill his TB medicines here - told them those come through the health department program.

reports.text: PA and lateral chest compared with 10/27/2020. The right apical airspace opacity has resolved. Minimal linear scarring at the right apex. No cavitation. Lungs otherwise clear. No effusion. Heart size normal.
reports.conclusion: Resolved right apical infiltrate with minimal residual apical scarring.

documents.title: Infectious Disease final visit
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
ID clinic, seen 05/14/2021.
Six months of therapy for drug-susceptible pulmonary TB completed today by DOT (2 months HRZE, 4 months HR). Weight regained, appetite normal, no cough or fever. End-of-treatment chest film 5/11: infiltrate resolved, minimal residual scarring at the right apex.
Plan: stop isoniazid, rifampin and pyridoxine. Treatment complete; cured. No routine further sputum. Any new cough, fever or weight loss should prompt sputum AFB. Discharged from ID clinic. Copy to primary care, nephrology and the health department.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ID final letter in: TB treatment completed 5/14, film cleared, discharged from ID. Feels like himself again. Weight 83.5 kg. Sugars a touch lower since stopping rifampin, fasting 120s-170s. No lows.

Exam: BP R arm as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. No edema.

A/P
History of pulmonary TB, treated - problem list updated.
T2DM - A1c 7.9 in March; recheck at fall wellness visit. Same insulin.
Statin - lipids and liver tests today.
RTC September for AWV.

documents.body: Annual diabetic eye exam 7/6/2021. No diabetic retinopathy OU. Color vision normal (patient mentioned prior ethambutol). Cataracts mild, stable. Recall 1 year.

documents.body: Reminder: your annual wellness visit is Tuesday 9/14 at 9:00. Please bring your glucose meter and all medicines, including the ones from the kidney doctor.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV.
Function: independent. Stopped driving to dialysis this year; uses the county ride service or his daughter. No falls. PHQ-2 1 (some days low energy, not low mood). Recall 3/3.
Meds reviewed: glargine 24 u qhs, lispro scale, lisinopril 5, sevelamer 800 with meals, aspirin 81, atorvastatin 40; epoetin at dialysis.
Exam: BP R arm as charted. Lungs clear. Feet: intact skin, sensation normal, pulses palpable.
Prevention: colonoscopy 2015 normal. Shingrix done. Pneumococcal done. COVID x2 - booster when eligible. Flu next month. Eye exam July, no retinopathy. Lung screening paused during TB; resume with LDCT this winter.
Labs: A1c, CBC.

documents.title: Vaccine visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high-dose) and Pfizer booster, both right arm, separate sites (no BP/injections left arm - fistula). Observed 15 min. Fine.
